matches.answer: Begin drying as soon as practical after harvest. Dry the grain evenly to a safe moisture level suitable for storage or milling.

results.question: How can I process palm fruits into oil at home?
results.expected_answer: To process palm oil at home: harvest fresh bunches and ferment for 3-5 days to loosen fruits, thresh fruits from the bunch, boil fruits for 30-60 minutes until soft, pound or press to separate oil from fiber, add water and boil the pulp again, skim oil from the surface, filter through cloth, boil the filtered oil to remove water (until bubbling stops), and cool before storing in sealed containers. Traditional palm press improves extraction efficiency.

matches.question: how can i process coconut into different products?
matches.answer: Coconut can be processed into coconut oil by grating mature coconut extracting the milk and boiling until oil separates, coconut cream and milk for cooking, desiccated coconut from dried grated flesh, coconut shell charcoal and crafts, coconut fibre from the husk for mats and ropes, and coconut water which is a popular beverage. In coastal Ghana there is good market for fresh coconuts coconut oil and coconut water. Value addition significantly increases income from coconut farming.

matches.question: how can i make compost at home?
matches.answer: Mix green materials like grass and vegetable waste with brown materials like dry leaves and straw in a pile. Keep it moist and turn it every 2 weeks. After 2-3 months, you will have rich compost ready for your farm.

matches.question: how can i make neem pesticide at home?
matches.answer: Crush 500g of neem seeds, soak in 10 litres of water overnight, strain through cloth, and add a little soap. Spray on crops in early morning or evening. Neem controls aphids, whiteflies, and caterpillars. Reapply after rain.

results.question: How can trees support a farm?
results.expected_answer: Trees can provide shade, wind protection, organic matter and products such as fruit or timber, while suitable agroforestry can improve farm resilience.

matches.question: how can water harvesting support dry-season farming?
matches.answer: Stored water can supplement irrigation during dry periods when designed and managed safely.

matches.question: how should i grow coconut trees in ghana?
matches.answer: Coconut grows best along coastal areas and in areas with high rainfall. Plant whole mature coconuts or purchase nursery seedlings. Dig a hole 1 metre deep and wide, add compost to the base and plant the seedling. Space at 7 to 10 metres apart. Coconut begins bearing fruit after 6 to 10 years depending on variety. Dwarf varieties like Malayan Dwarf produce earlier at 3 to 4 years. Apply potassium-rich fertilizer for good fruit production.

matches.question: how often should i inspect cocoa trees?
matches.answer: Inspect regularly for pests, diseases, damaged branches, weeds and moisture stress. Early detection makes management easier.

results.question: When should I harvest sorghum?
results.expected_answer: Harvest sorghum when grain is hard, heads have turned their mature color, and moisture content is around 20-25%. Dry after harvest before storage. Harvest promptly to avoid bird damage.

matches.question: when should i harvest tomatoes?
matches.answer: Harvest tomatoes when they are fully colored but still firm. For selling to distant markets, harvest at the breaker stage when they begin to change color so they ripen during transport without getting damaged.

matches.question: when should i harvest tilapia?
matches.answer: Harvest tilapia when they reach market size of 300 to 500 grams which typically takes 5 to 6 months from fingerling stage. Monitor growth by sampling fish monthly using a net. Harvest in the early morning when water temperature is cool to reduce fish stress. Partial harvesting at 4 months removes larger fish and allows smaller ones to grow. Sell fresh fish immediately or ice them for transport to market.

matches.question: when should i harvest groundnuts?
matches.answer: Harvest groundnuts when leaves start yellowing. Loosen the soil with a hoe first then pull the whole plant upward. Shake off excess soil and thresh on a clean tarpaulin. Dry pods in the sun for 3-5 days before storage.

results.question: How long can fresh cassava be stored after harvest?
results.expected_answer: Fresh cassava deteriorates within 24-72 hours after harvest. For longer storage, process into dried chips, gari, or flour. Waxing the roots can extend fresh storage to about a week. Keep in cool, shaded areas.

matches.question: how should honey be stored?
matches.answer: Store honey in clean, food-grade containers in a dry place away from strong odours and excess moisture.

matches.question: how should farm machinery be stored?
matches.answer: Keep equipment clean, dry, sheltered and secure, and follow the manufacturer's maintenance schedule.

matches.question: how should cucumbers be handled after harvest?
matches.answer: Handle them gently, keep them shaded and avoid excessive heat to preserve freshness and reduce bruising.

results.question: How can I grow cocoyam successfully in Ghana?
results.expected_answer: Cocoyam grows best in moist fertile soils with partial shade. Plant corms or cormels at a depth of 5 to 10 cm and spacing of 60 by 60 cm. It performs well under banana or plantain canopies. Apply organic matter at planting. Cocoyam requires regular watering during dry periods and takes 7 to 12 months to mature depending on variety. Taro cocoyam and Tannia are the two main types grown in Ghana.

matches.question: how can i grow carrots successfully in ghana?
matches.answer: Carrots grow best in loose, deep, stone-free sandy loam soils. Prepare the bed by digging deep to at least 30 cm and removing stones and clods. Sow seeds directly in rows 20 cm apart at a depth of 1 cm. Thin seedlings to 5 to 8 cm apart after germination. Apply phosphorus-rich fertilizer at planting. Carrots need consistent moisture but not waterlogging. They are ready to harvest in 70 to 80 days.

matches.question: how do i grow onions successfully in ghana?
matches.answer: Onions grow best in the dry season under irrigation especially in northern Ghana. Raise seedlings in a nursery for 6 to 8 weeks before transplanting. Prepare well-drained raised beds with compost. Transplant seedlings 10 to 15 cm apart. Apply NPK fertilizer at transplanting and nitrogen top dressing at 3 weeks. Keep the field weed-free. Onions are ready in 90 to 120 days. Cure harvested bulbs in the shade for 2 weeks before storage.

matches.question: how do i grow garden eggs successfully in ghana?
matches.answer: Garden eggs also called African eggplant are popular in Ghana. Start seedlings in a nursery for 4 weeks. Transplant to the field at 60 by 60 cm spacing. Apply compost at planting and NPK fertilizer at 3 weeks after transplanting. Control the epilachna beetle which is the most destructive pest by hand picking or using neem extract. Garden eggs mature in 60 to 90 days and can be harvested multiple times from the same plant.

results.question: What minimum pond size is suitable for commercial fish farming?
results.expected_answer: For commercial fish farming the minimum recommended pond size is 500 square metres. This size allows you to stock approximately 1,500 to 2,500 tilapia or 5,000 to 10,000 catfish fingerlings. Smaller ponds are possible but make it harder to achieve economies of scale and recover your investment. Ideally a commercial fish farm should have at least 2 to 3 ponds to allow rotation for pond maintenance and continuous production and staggered harvesting for regular income.

matches.question: what crop rotation plan is suitable for ghana?
matches.answer: A good crop rotation for Ghana is to plant legumes like cowpea or groundnut after cereals like maize or sorghum. Legumes fix nitrogen into the soil improving fertility naturally. A 3-year rotation could be maize in year one, cowpea in year two, and cassava or vegetables in year three. Avoid planting the same crop family in the same field two seasons in a row as this builds up pests and diseases specific to that crop.

matches.question: what kind of site is suitable for cucumber?
matches.answer: Choose a sunny site with fertile, well-drained soil and access to reliable water.

matches.question: which fodder crops are suitable for cattle in ghana?
matches.answer: Good fodder crops for cattle in Ghana include Napier grass which produces high biomass and can be harvested every 6 to 8 weeks, Guinea grass, Stylosanthes guianensis which is a nutritious legume that fixes nitrogen, Centrosema which is a climbing legume, Leucaena trees which provide protein-rich pods and leaves, and Mucuna which is an excellent dry season fodder. Establish a fodder plot of at least 0.5 hectares per cow. Cut and carry feed to cattle rather than letting them graze uncontrolled to improve feed efficiency.

results.question: How can rabbit production be made more profitable?
results.expected_answer: Control feed costs, reduce mortality, maintain good breeding performance, keep records and target reliable markets.

matches.question: how can i make tomato farming profitable?
matches.answer: To make profit from tomatoes, time your production to sell when prices are high which is usually the dry season from November to February. Use drip irrigation for dry season production. Produce in bulk to negotiate better prices, form a farmer group to collectively market your tomatoes, and consider simple processing like tomato paste or puree to add value and extend shelf life. Keep detailed records of all costs.

matches.question: how should rabbit manure be handled?
matches.answer: Collect it regularly and compost or manage it appropriately before applying it to crops.

matches.question: how can i make my farming business more climate-smart?
matches.answer: Practice climate-smart farming by planting trees on your farm through agroforestry, using compost and manure instead of chemical fertilizers, practicing minimum tillage to protect soil carbon, using water-efficient irrigation, growing diverse crops, and avoiding burning crop residues.

results.question: What are whiteflies and how can I remove them from my crops?
results.expected_answer: Whiteflies are tiny white insects that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Control them by spraying insecticidal soap, neem oil, or imidacloprid. Yellow sticky traps also help. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer which attracts them.

matches.question: what are whiteflies and how can i get rid of them?
matches.answer: Whiteflies are tiny white insects that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Control them by spraying insecticidal soap, neem oil, or imidacloprid. Yellow sticky traps also help. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer which attracts them.

matches.question: how can i prevent pests from attacking my crops?
matches.answer: Practice crop rotation, remove crop residues after harvest, use pest-resistant varieties, plant trap crops like marigolds, use nets or row covers, and monitor your farm regularly.

matches.question: what are the major risks in farming and how can i manage them?
matches.answer: Main farming risks include weather risks from drought or flooding, pest and disease outbreaks, price volatility at harvest time, input price increases, land tenure insecurity, and lack of market access. Manage these risks by diversifying crops so one failure does not ruin you entirely, using drought-resistant varieties, taking out crop insurance where available, joining farmer groups for collective bargaining, storing produce to sell when prices improve, securing formal land documents, and building relationships with multiple buyers.

results.question: What is the difference between tilapia and catfish farming?
results.expected_answer: Tilapia is easier to manage, tolerates lower water quality, feeds on plankton and algae as well as pellets, and is cheaper to produce. Catfish grows faster, commands a higher market price, tolerates very low oxygen levels but needs more protein in feed. Catfish farming gives higher profit per fish but requires more management. Many farmers in Ghana combine both species for diversified income.

matches.question: what is the difference between sheep farming and goat farming?
matches.answer: Sheep are grazers that prefer grass while goats are browsers that eat leaves and shrubs. Sheep are generally more docile and easier to manage in groups. Goats are more curious and tend to escape from enclosures. Goat meat commands a slightly higher price in Ghanaian markets. Sheep wool is not commercially harvested in Ghana as local breeds have hair not wool. Both require similar health management including PPR vaccination.

matches.question: what is the difference between plantain farming and banana farming?
matches.answer: Plantain and banana are closely related but differ in use and management. Plantain is starchier, larger and must be cooked before eating. Banana is sweeter, eaten raw and matures faster. Banana requires more water and is more sensitive to drought. Plantain is more tolerant of less fertile soils. Both need similar disease management. Commercial banana farming for export requires higher standards of pest and disease control.

matches.question: what is the difference between upland and lowland rice farming?
matches.answer: Upland rice is grown without standing water, while lowland rice is grown where water can be managed in low-lying fields. The suitable system depends on rainfall, soil and water availability.

results.question: When should I deworm cattle and what should I use?
results.expected_answer: Deworm cattle every 3 to 4 months using broad-spectrum anthelmintics like Ivermectin which controls both internal and external parasites, Albendazole or Levamisole. Deworm at the start of the rainy season when parasite burden peaks and again at the start of the dry season. Always weigh or estimate the body weight of each animal to administer the correct dose. Underdosing causes resistance. Rotate between dewormers annually. Calves need more frequent deworming every 6 to 8 weeks.

matches.question: what is a nursery and when should i use one?
matches.answer: A nursery is a protected area where seeds are germinated and young plants are raised before transplanting to the main field. Use a nursery for: small expensive seeds like tomato, pepper, and onion; crops that need a head start before rains; and crops where seedling survival in the field is uncertain. Nurseries save seeds and improve stand establishment.

matches.question: what spacing should i use when planting maize?
matches.answer: Use a spacing of 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between plants within the row. Plant 2 seeds per hole at a depth of 3 to 5 cm. After germination, thin to one strong plant per stand. This spacing allows each plant enough space, sunlight and nutrients to grow well.

matches.question: when should i harvest tomatoes?
matches.answer: Harvest tomatoes when they are fully colored but still firm. For selling to distant markets, harvest at the breaker stage when they begin to change color so they ripen during transport without getting damaged.

results.question: What can snails eat on a farm?
results.expected_answer: Provide suitable fresh plant materials and balanced supplementary feed appropriate for the farming system.

matches.question: why is traceability useful on a farm?
matches.answer: Simple records can help identify where produce came from, how it was produced and where it was sold if a quality problem occurs.

matches.question: how does planting trees on a farm help reduce climate change?
matches.answer: Trees absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it in their wood and roots — this is called carbon sequestration. A single large tree can absorb 22 kg of carbon dioxide per year. Trees also reduce local temperatures, increase rainfall through transpiration, protect water catchments, and reduce erosion. Planting trees on your farm is one of the most powerful climate actions a farmer can take.

matches.question: how can i protect snails from predators?
matches.answer: Use secure housing, mesh or barriers and check regularly for ants, rodents, birds and other predators.

results.question: How can I tell whether snails are growing well?
results.expected_answer: Monitor shell development, body size, feeding activity and survival over time.

matches.question: how can i tell if chickens are eating normally?
matches.answer: Monitor feed consumption, activity, droppings, body condition and changes in behaviour rather than relying on one sign.

matches.question: how can i tell when my crops are lacking nutrients?
matches.answer: Common deficiency signs: Nitrogen deficiency — older leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom of the plant. Iron deficiency — young leaves turn yellow but veins stay green. Phosphorus deficiency — leaves turn purple or reddish. Potassium deficiency — leaf edges turn brown and crispy. Calcium deficiency — new leaves distort and curl. A soil test will confirm which nutrients are lacking.

matches.question: how can i tell if stored grain may have a mould problem?
matches.answer: Look for visible mould, unusual smell, clumping, discolouration or increased moisture. Suspect grain should be isolated and assessed.

results.question: Why are farmer field demonstrations useful?
results.expected_answer: Demonstrations allow farmers to see a practice under local conditions and compare results with familiar methods.

matches.question: why are watermelon fruits cracking?
matches.answer: Sudden changes in water availability, heavy rain after dry conditions and other stress can contribute to cracking.

matches.question: why are flowering plants important for bees?
matches.answer: Bees depend on flowers for nectar and pollen, so a variety of flowering plants can support colony development.

matches.question: why are my okra pods becoming hard?
matches.answer: Pods become hard when they stay on the plant too long. Harvest them while they are still young and tender.

results.question: How should breeding rabbits be selected?
results.expected_answer: Choose healthy animals with good body condition, sound feet and a history of good growth or reproduction.

matches.question: how should breeding grasscutters be selected?
matches.answer: Choose healthy animals with good body condition, sound movement and good reproductive records where available.

matches.question: why should rabbits not be kept in dirty cages?
matches.answer: Dirty housing increases odour, parasites and disease risks and can reduce animal performance.

matches.question: how can i reduce heat stress in rabbits?
matches.answer: Provide shade, ventilation, clean water and protect cages from direct heat during hot periods.

results.question: How do I set up a brooder for day-old chicks?
results.expected_answer: A brooder provides warmth for day-old chicks in the first 2 to 3 weeks. Use a heat lamp or electric bulb hung 45 cm above the floor in a circular guard made from cardboard or wire. Maintain temperature at 35 degrees Celsius in week one reducing by 3 degrees each week. Spread wood shavings as litter 5 to 7 cm deep. Provide water in chick-sized drinkers and starter feed in shallow trays. Watch chick behaviour to adjust temperature correctly.

matches.question: how can i set a fair price for my farm produce?
matches.answer: To price fairly, calculate your total production cost per unit (cost of seeds, fertilizer, labor, transport, etc. divided by total harvest). Add a profit margin of at least 20-30%. Check current market prices for similar produce in your area. Your price should cover all costs plus give you profit. Never sell below your production cost even if market prices are low.

matches.question: what time of day is best for harvesting vegetables?
matches.answer: Harvest vegetables in the early morning when temperatures are cool. This helps produce stay fresh longer. Avoid harvesting in midday heat. For leafy vegetables, harvest with dew still present for crispness.

matches.question: when should i remove old plantain leaves?
matches.answer: Remove dead or severely damaged leaves when necessary while avoiding excessive removal of healthy leaves.

results.question: How can I protect my farm from theft?
results.expected_answer: Protect your farm by: building proper fencing with thorny hedges or wire fencing, using watchdogs especially at harvest time, forming community vigilance groups with neighboring farmers, harvesting promptly when crops are ready to minimize field time after ripening, installing basic alarm systems if affordable, registering your farm to establish legal ownership, and developing good relationships with neighboring community members.

matches.question: how can i protect my farm from flooding and waterlogging?
matches.answer: Protect your farm from flooding and waterlogging by planting on raised beds or ridges especially for vegetables and root crops, digging drainage channels around the field perimeter to direct excess water away, avoiding farming in flood-prone low-lying areas during heavy rain seasons, choosing flood-tolerant varieties where possible, using cover crops and mulching to reduce runoff, and planting trees or grass strips along slopes to slow water flow and reduce erosion.

matches.question: how can i protect my farm during drought?
matches.answer: During drought, mulch heavily to conserve soil moisture, irrigate if possible, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and avoid adding nitrogen fertilizer which increases water demand. Harvest early-maturing varieties before drought peaks.

matches.question: how can i protect my rice from birds?
matches.answer: Use bird scaring methods: move scarecrows regularly to remain effective, hang reflective tape or old CDs around the field, use noise-makers, and recruit children to chase birds during grain-filling stage. Growing early-maturing varieties reduces the bird damage period.

results.question: What is Fall Armyworm and how can I control it?
results.expected_answer: Fall Armyworm is a highly destructive caterpillar that mainly attacks maize. It can destroy an entire field within days. Control with insecticides like emamectin benzoate, apply early morning, and target the whorls where larvae hide.

matches.question: what is fall armyworm and what does it do to maize?
matches.answer: Fall Armyworm is a highly destructive caterpillar that mainly attacks maize. It can destroy an entire field within days. Control with insecticides like emamectin benzoate, apply early morning, and target the whorls where larvae hide.

matches.question: what is striga and how can i control it?
matches.answer: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches to crop roots. Control includes using Striga-resistant varieties, applying Imazapyr-coated seeds, hand pulling Striga before it flowers, growing trap crops like Sudan grass, and applying fertilizer to help crops outcompete Striga.

matches.question: what is powdery mildew and how can i control it?
matches.answer: Powdery mildew appears as white powdery patches on leaves and stems. It is caused by fungi and thrives in warm, dry conditions with high humidity. It weakens plants and reduces yield. Control by: removing infected leaves, improving air circulation by pruning, spraying with diluted baking soda solution (1 tablespoon per litre of water), neem oil, or sulfur-based fungicides.

results.question: How can I control Panama disease in plantain and banana?
results.expected_answer: Panama disease is a fatal fungal soil disease. Use certified disease-free planting material, avoid planting in previously infected soil, practice strict hygiene by cleaning tools before moving between farms, and plant resistant varieties like Cardaba or FHIA hybrids. There is no chemical cure.

matches.question: how can i control black sigatoka disease in plantain?
matches.answer: Black sigatoka is a serious fungal disease causing black streaks on leaves that eventually kill them. Control it by removing and destroying affected leaves regularly, ensuring good drainage, maintaining adequate spacing for air circulation, and applying recommended fungicides like Mancozeb or Dithane every 2 to 3 weeks during wet seasons. Use resistant varieties like Apantu and FHIA-21 where available.

matches.question: what is the difference between plantain farming and banana farming?
matches.answer: Plantain and banana are closely related but differ in use and management. Plantain is starchier, larger and must be cooked before eating. Banana is sweeter, eaten raw and matures faster. Banana requires more water and is more sensitive to drought. Plantain is more tolerant of less fertile soils. Both need similar disease management. Commercial banana farming for export requires higher standards of pest and disease control.

matches.question: how can i prevent newcastle disease in poultry?
matches.answer: Newcastle disease is the most serious threat to poultry in Ghana. Prevent it through strict vaccination using Lasota vaccine at day 7, day 21 and every 2 months thereafter. Keep visitors away from your poultry house, disinfect equipment and footwear before entering, quarantine new birds for 2 weeks, buy birds from certified sources only, and cull sick birds immediately. There is no treatment for Newcastle disease once birds are infected.

results.question: What should I do if my farm becomes waterlogged?
results.expected_answer: If your farm floods regularly, take these steps: dig drainage channels around and through the field to direct water away, create raised beds to keep plant roots above waterline, plant flood-tolerant crop varieties, install water pumps to remove standing water quickly, build earthen bunds around the field perimeter, and consider planting floating rice varieties if flooding is very severe and frequent.

matches.question: what should i do if fish stop feeding suddenly?
matches.answer: Check water quality, temperature, oxygen, recent weather, feed quality and signs of disease before increasing feed.

matches.question: what should i do if someone is poisoned by pesticide?
matches.answer: If pesticide poisoning occurs: call the Ghana Poisons Information Centre or the nearest hospital immediately, remove the victim from the exposure area, if ingested do not induce vomiting unless directed by medical professionals, if on skin remove contaminated clothing and wash with soap and water, if in eyes flush with clean water for 15-20 minutes, bring the pesticide container or label to the hospital. Prevention: always wear protective equipment when using pesticides.

matches.question: how do i know if my fertilizer is working?
matches.answer: Signs that fertilizer is working include: darker green leaves, faster plant growth, larger leaves, and higher yield compared to unfertilized plots. If plants remain yellowish and grow slowly after 2-3 weeks of fertilizer application, the fertilizer may not have been applied correctly or the soil may have other problems.

results.question: What equipment do I need to start a small farm?
results.expected_answer: Essential tools for smallholder farming include a hoe and cutlass for land preparation and weeding, a watering can for irrigation, a knapsack sprayer for pesticide application, a measuring tape, storage bags including hermetic bags for grain, and a simple scale.

matches.question: how do i start a small rabbit farm?
matches.answer: Begin with healthy breeding stock, suitable housing, reliable feed and water, a cleaning routine and a simple production record system.

matches.question: how much does it cost to start a small fish farm in ghana?
matches.answer: Starting a small commercial fish farm in Ghana with two earthen ponds of 500 square metres each costs approximately GHS 15,000 to 25,000 including pond construction, fingerlings, feed for one cycle, and basic equipment. A plastic tank fish farm can be started for GHS 8,000 to 15,000. The main ongoing costs are fish feed which accounts for 60 to 70 percent of total production cost. With good management you can make a profit from the first cycle.

matches.question: what licence do i need to sell agricultural chemicals in ghana?
matches.answer: To sell agricultural chemicals (pesticides, fertilizers) in Ghana, you need: a license from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which requires completing a training course on pesticide handling, passing an examination, paying the licensing fee, having appropriate storage facilities, and renewing the license annually. Selling agricultural chemicals without a license is illegal and carries penalties. Contact the EPA Pesticides Control and Management Centre for the application process.

results.question: Why should cucumber farmers avoid planting the crop repeatedly in the same spot?
results.expected_answer: Rotation reduces the buildup of pests and diseases that remain in the soil and helps maintain better field health.

matches.question: when should cucumber be harvested?
matches.answer: Harvest when fruits have reached the market size and are still firm and tender. Delayed harvesting can reduce quality.

matches.question: why should i record crop failures?
matches.answer: Recording failures helps identify repeated problems such as pests, poor timing, drought, disease or unsuitable varieties.

matches.question: how often should cucumber be picked?
matches.answer: Pick frequently during the production period so mature fruits do not remain on the vines and slow further production.

results.question: How deep should I plant maize seeds?
results.expected_answer: Plant maize seeds 3-5 cm deep. If the soil is dry, plant slightly deeper to reach moisture. Space seeds 25-30 cm apart within rows and 75-90 cm between rows.

matches.question: when is the best time to plant maize in ghana?
matches.answer: In Ghana, the best time to plant maize is at the beginning of the rainy season — March to April in the south, and May to June in the north. Plant when you have received at least 2-3 good rains so the soil is well moistened.

matches.question: how should i plant crops on slopes to prevent water erosion?
matches.answer: On slopes, always plant across the slope (contour planting) rather than up and down. Make ridges along contour lines to hold water. Plant cover crops or grasses on the steepest parts. Use tied ridges (ridges with cross-ties every few meters) to capture rainwater. Mulch heavily to protect soil between plants.

matches.question: dɛn na nnuaba-mfoforo wu yadeɛ yadeɛ yɛ wɔ nnuaba mfoforo mu?

matches.question: dɛn na nhwiren-tew ferefere yɛ na ɛdeɛn na mefa di dwuma?

matches.answer: NPK kyerɛ Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), ne Potassium (K) — aduan titiriw mmiɛnsa a nnuaba hia. Nitrogen boa nhaban da sor, Phosphorus boa ntini ne abode, na Potassium ma tibo yɛ den na aba yɛ pa. Nɔma te sɛ 15-15-15 no kyerɛ kɛse a aduan biara wɔ bag mu.

matches.question: ɛdeɛn na mepaw aba pa sɛ mede to mu?
matches.answer: Paw aba a wɔakyerɛw won fi agro-input atɔfo a wɔn din ayɛ pa. Aba pa yɛ pɛ wɔ boɔ mu, wɔ mfomso, na wɔn nyini yɛ kɛse sen 85%. Bɔ hwɛ de aba a wogye fi dɛm nnuaba meto aba hybrid aba no ase.

matches.question: ɛkwan pa bɛn na mede bayerɛ twew na guina yi akyi?
matches.answer: Bayerɛ twew yi akyi boa sɛ nsono ketewa wɔ ho so sa na aguina bere tenten. De bayerɛ a woyii sie wɔ baabi a ɛhyehyɛ kakra ne nsuo wɔ mu wɔ degrees 29 kɔ 35 Celsius ne relative humidity 90 kɔ 95 percent mu adays nnan kɔ nwɔtwe. Bayerɛ a woguina yie tena agyapade mmiɛnsa kɔ nsia mu.

results.question: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick nnuaba pa ma me asase nhyiamu?
results.expected_answer: De wo nnuaba hyɛ wo asase nhyiamu mu ma nnoa pa. Sandy asase sua nsuo ntɛm na ɛbɛn groundnut, bɔde, sweet potato ne watermelon. Clay asase kora nsuo na ɛbɛn ɔmo, taro cocoyam ne nnuaba bi. Loam asase ne asase a ɛbɛn nnuaba bebree a aburoɔ, bankye, tomatoes ne nnuaba bebree ka ho. Gye wo asase hwɛ fi wo MOFA ofisi a ɛbɛn anaa agricultural laboratory ma wohunu wo asase pH ne ferefere levels ansa na wopick wo nnuaba.

matches.question: dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mepick aburoɔ aba variety pa wɔ me ɛhɔ ho?
matches.answer: Yi wo aburoɔ variety sɛ nsuo a ɛtɔ bere wɔ wo hɔ, asase nhyiamu, na wo dwa so. Ma kwaeɛ zone a nsuo tɔ pii ho, de medium kɔ late maturing varieties te sɛ Abontem anaa Mamaba. Ma mmoa aduan, yellow varieties te sɛ Dobidi wɔ energy pii mu. Gye certified seed fi licensed dealers.

matches.question: dɛn na menyɛ compost ma me aburoɔ afuom?
matches.answer: Yɛ compost de layers a nnuaba a ato fɛw aba ntama a wɔatew te sɛ aburoɔ abɔ ka ho ne nnuaba foforɔ te sɛ nhawan ne efie ho nneɛma. De asase ketewa anaa compost a ɛawie to ntam biara mu sɛ ɛde organisms a ɛhia kɔ. Ma pile no nsuo ho kakra nanso nsuo nni mu agyina na gyinaso mprɛn mmienu biara nnansas. Compost no atwa so nnansas nwɔtwe kɔ duonum mmienu mu bere a ɛyɛ dark brown, ɛpepee yie na ɛwɔ nhwirɛ pa. De compost tonnes mmienu kɔ mmiɛnsa to eka baako so ansa na wode aba to mu sɛ ɛboa asase aduan pii.

results.question: Mɛyɛ dɛn akora nsɛm wɔ cocoa afuo ho?
results.expected_answer: Kyerɛw asase a wodua so, adwumayɛfo, nneɛma a wode di dwuma, aba dodow, tɔn, yare ho nsɛm ne sika a wode yɛɛ adwuma sɛnea wobɛtumi de akyerɛw seasons no toto ho.

matches.question: mɛyɛ dɛn ama cocoa afuo no ho atew?
matches.answer: Yi nwura a ɛdɔɔso, nneɛma a awu ne afã a yare aka ho yiye. Ma akwan a wokɔ so yɛ mmerɛ sɛ wobɛhwɛ nnua no na woagye aba.

matches.question: ɛdeɛn na melem m'afuo ho mfaaso?
matches.answer: Mfaaso yɛ sika nyinaa a wogye fi tɔn no minus sika nyinaa a wode. Kora sika nyinaa a wode ka ho te sɛ aba, ferefere, dwumadie, kwan so sika, dawuro, ne sika nyinaa a wogye fi tɔn. Kora krataa ketewa anaa fa wo fɔn de kora da biara ho sika.

matches.question: ɛho hia sɛn ara sɛ wɔkora nsɛm wɔ afuom adwuma mu?
matches.answer: Nsɛm kora ho hia pa ara ma afuom adwuma bo so. Kora nsɛm ho sɛ inputs nyinaa a wagye ne sika, to aba bere ne dodoɔ, adwuma sika, nnoa a afuom biara fi, tɔ sika ne buyer ho nsɛm, na mmoa health ho nsɛm. Nsɛm a wɔakora yie boa wo sɛ wobɛbu real mfaso, hunu biribi a ɛyɛ yie ne a ɛnyɛ yie, twerɛ bo sɛ bank loans hia, siesie wo adwuma yie ma bere a ɛdi hɔ, na tia certification ho nhia sɛ wopɛ sɛ wotɔ kɔ premium markets.

results.question: Ɛdeɛn na mekura kakaduro yie?
results.expected_answer: Kakaduro da sor pa wɔ beae a owia tra mu kakra na ɛwɔ huhu, asase a ɛwɔ aduan pa na nsuo pue mu yie. De rhizomes to asase mu sɛntimita 5-7 na gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 20-30. Kora asase nte na de mulch to so papaapa. Gye abosome 8-10 akyi a nhaban no dan sika na awu.

matches.question: ɛdeɛn na mekura watermelon yie?
matches.answer: Watermelon hia asintiɛ asase a nsuo pue mu yie, owia mu, na owia hye pa. Gyae asukyerɛ mita 1.5-2. De nsuo to asase mu yiye nanso mmere pii bi. De potassium ferefere to so bere a aba reba. Gye bere a ntini a ɛbɛn aba no dan ɛda.

matches.question: ɛdeɛn na mekura cashew yie?
matches.answer: Cashew da sor pa wɔ asase a nsuo pue mu yie a ɛyɛ asintiɛ anaa laterite wɔ beae a ɔpɛ bere wɔ hɔ. To aba tɔtɔ wɔ asase mu sɛntimita 5 anaa si nnuaba mfoforo ananmu. Gyae nnua asukyerɛ mita 8-10. De ferefere to mfe a ɛto so abien ananmu. Kora collar rot yadeɛ, cashew tibo ne ntini adwummakers, ne anthracnose ase. Gye aba bere a cashew apple no dan hoho anaa kɔkɔɔ na aba no dan tuntum-brɔdwa. Cashew nnua da sor fi mfe 3-5 akyi.

matches.question: ɛdeɛn na mekura aborɔfo wɔ adwuma mu?
matches.answer: Aborɔfo adwuma kura ho: to suckers anaa crowns fi nnua a wɔwɔ aho wɔ, gyae asukyerɛ sɛntimita 60x30 wɔ asase-sor afuo wɔ nnua so mu, de NPK ferefere to mprɛ mmiɛnsa bere biara, ma abode ba wɔ de ethephon anaa acetylene solution hyɛ wɔ bosome 12-14 akyi sɛ wogye bere koro, kora mealy bug ne heart rot yadeɛ ase, gye bosome 15-18 akyi a wode to mu. MD2 ne Smooth Cayenne yɛ export aba a wɔpɛ wɔn. Ghana de aborɔfo kɔ Yurop dodo.

results.question: Dɛn na menyɛ sɛ mebisa Planting for Food and Jobs programme?
results.expected_answer: Sɛ wobɛbisa Planting for Food and Jobs programme a, kɔ wo District Department of Agriculture ofisi a ɛbɛn wo wɔ Ministry of Food and Agriculture ase. De wo Ghana Card, asase ho evidence anaa asase de adi nhyiamu krataa, na wo afuom hɔ. Si ho sɛ beneficiary okuafo. Inputs a wɔde asua te sɛ aba ne ferefere na wɔde kyɛ wɔ licensed agro-dealers mu wɔ wo district mu. Programme no fa aburoɔ, ɔmo, soybean, sorghum, nnuaba ne nnuaba foforɔ ho.

matches.question: dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meto abɔnkɔ wɔ ghana?
matches.answer: Abɔnkɔ to yie wɔ bone berɛ wɔ quench ase a ɛhia pii wɔ Ghana atifi. Ma seedlings so wɔ nursery nnansa nsia kɔ nwɔtwe ansa na wode transplant. Siesie beds a ɛtele ne nsuo tew ne compost a ɛwɔ mu. Transplant seedlings sɛntimita 10 kɔ 15 ntam. De NPK ferefere to ho bere a wode transplant na nitrogen top dressing nnansa mmiɛnsa mu. Kora afuom no ho nhaban foforo mu. Abɔnkɔ atwa so adays 90 kɔ 120 mu. Twew bulbs a woyii no wɔ hare ha mprɛnsa mmienu ansa na woguina mu.

matches.question: dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meto ntorɔ wɔ ghana?
matches.answer: Ntorɔ a wɔfre no African eggplant nso ne aduan a wɔpɛ wɔ Ghana. Fi ase de aba to mu wɔ nursery nnansa nnan. Transplant kɔ afuom wɔ ahodɔ 60 ne 60 sɛntimita. Ntorɔ twa so sɛ wɔbɛyi adays 60 kɔ 90 mu na wubetumi ayi fi nnuaba koro mu daa.

matches.question: dɛn na menyɛ sɛ meto carrot wɔ ghana?

matches.question: sacks aburoɔ ahe na mebetumi anya fi eka baako mu?

Asɛde a ɛma aburoɔ rebɛ yɛ ne: asase no aduan, aba variety, bere pa mu to aba, nhaban foforo yi, adwummaker hwɛ, na nsuo pa.

matches.question: mfa sika ahe bɛfata me wɔ bankye eka baako mu?

Bankye adwuma ho bo tɔ sen a wode ayɛ gari, starch anaa fufu flour ansa na wotɔ.
